questionText:
Read the passage and answer the questions:
 
 Charkha
 
What I object to, is the craze for machinery as such. The craze is for what
they call labour-saving machinery. Men go on “saving labour”, till
thousands are without work and thrown on the open streets to die of
starvation. I want to save time and labour, not for a fraction of mankind, but
for all; I want the concentration of wealth, not in the hands of few, but in the
hands of all.
 
 YOUNG INDIA, 13 NOVEMBER 1924
Khaddar does not seek to destroy all machinery but it does regulate its use
and check its weedy growth. It uses machinery for the service of the
poorest in their own cottages. The wheel is itself an exquisite piece of
machinery.
 
 YOUNG INDIA, 17 MARCH 1927
What does the writer mean by 'saving labour'?
